name: FillMatic
outcome: Turns repetitive test-data entry into a reusable one-click workflow.
description: A Chrome extension that fills real-world web forms with realistic test data in one click, including the controls most autofill tools miss.

highlights: One-click realistic names, emails, addresses, dates, phone numbers, and payment test data, plus a repeat of the last fill that survives reloads
Framework-aware writes keep React and Vue-style controlled inputs in sync
Drives ARIA comboboxes, calendars, switches, sliders, and radio groups like a user would
Rich-text support for ProseMirror, Lexical, Slate, Quill, Trix, and contenteditable
Record a Recipe by using a widget once: clicks, keys, and waits become safe declarative steps, with no eval or remote code
Profiles, Actions, and Recipes turn repeated test flows into reusable workflows, built with an element picker and live on-page step outlines
Built-in Stripe test-card Actions for success, declined, and 3D Secure flows that only appear on test-mode checkouts
Field detection reads labels in English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, and Japanese
Fill-only by default: ignore fields or whole containers by word or CSS selector, fill a single field from the right-click menu, and never submit unless you turn that on
details.problem: Realistic form testing breaks down on modern UIs. Controlled React inputs ignore naive value writes, custom selects and date pickers are not real form controls, and checkout fields often mount only after you interact with the page. Testers end up retyping the same data by hand or maintaining brittle scripts.
details.architecture: A Chrome extension split across popup, settings, side panel, and a background service worker. Content scripts own every DOM mutation, one per frame. Fills run through an ordered strategy pipeline: native inputs first, then a DOM quiet-period and a second pass for late-mounted controls, then user Recipes, widget adapters, and editor-aware insertion. A failure on one element is logged and skipped instead of aborting the whole form. Everything lives in chrome.storage.local, with no application backend. The side panel hosts the Action and Recipe builders, where a recorder captures interactions on the page and turns them into reviewable steps. An experimental, off-by-default mapper can run Gemini Nano on-device through Chrome's Prompt API, and its output is saved as a normal Action, so running an Action never needs the model.
engineering: Failure-isolated pipeline: one broken field never takes down the rest of the form
Deterministic value resolution: Actions and profile rules outrank heuristics, so results are predictable
Automation health: every Action and Recipe reports when it last worked, or the exact step and reason it stopped
One URL matcher shared by Actions, Recipes, and Field rules, so an Action never runs on a page it no longer matches
Recipe imports are validated and reviewed before saving, all or nothing
Privacy by design: no application server, and on-device Gemini Nano means page contents are never transmitted for mapping
Typed, command-scoped messaging between extension contexts, with the fill engine loaded on demand
Tested in real Chromium with Playwright, including a real Radix Select, shadow DOM, and iframes
Enforced 90% coverage floors across statements, branches, functions, and lines
Tagged releases are tested, packaged, and published to the Chrome Web Store through CI

name: Polychat
outcome: Benchmarks models on speed and answer quality, blind, in one private workspace.
description: A local-first AI workspace for chatting with and evaluating LLMs side by side, with blind judging, speed metrics, and an encrypted bring-your-own-key vault.

highlights: Run one prompt against two to four models in parallel and compare time to first token, tokens per second, cost, and answer quality
Blind judging with rubric scores and a local win-rate leaderboard, so model names never bias the verdict
Saved prompt suites, run history, and JSON or CSV export for repeatable comparisons
Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, DeepSeek, and OpenRouter in one workspace, with models discovered from your own keys
Full chat workspace: per-thread profiles and languages, rich Markdown, image and video generation, and file attachments
Threads, history, and keys stay in your browser, with an encrypted BYOK vault and optional passkey unlock
details.problem: I built Polychat for my own model testing. When a new model ships, I use it to check how fast it really is and how good its answers are against the ones I already use, often through OpenRouter. Blind judging keeps the comparison honest, since I rate answers before seeing which model wrote them. It also replaces juggling separate provider apps, and keeps conversations and API keys on my device.
details.architecture: A React 19 and React Router 8 SPA with Jotai state and a TipTap composer. Threads, compare history, prompt suites, and the key vault persist locally in IndexedDB. Compare runs stream in parallel outside the chat queue, timing each answer as tokens arrive. A small Hono API on AWS Lambda authenticates Clerk JWTs and streams through the Vercel AI SDK, behind a Cloudflare Pages proxy secret. With a BYOK key, requests stream from the browser straight to the provider.
engineering: Speed metrics measured from the live stream, with reasoning tokens excluded from tokens per second
Per-column retry, so one failed model never forces a rerun of the others
Envelope encryption: provider keys sealed with a random AES-GCM vault key, wrapped by PBKDF2-SHA-256 (600,000 iterations)
Optional WebAuthn PRF device unlock, with passphrase recovery as the fallback, and no vault stored on the server
Type-safe model catalog: provider-compatible model IDs derived from the AI SDK types
Locked-down API: Clerk JWT checks with an authorized-parties allowlist, plus a proxy secret in production
